tonight.headline: McLaurin is expected to miss London; the flex now rests on Coker's quad
body: Bad news first. Terry McLaurin is now expected to miss Sunday's game in London: Ben Standig reported this morning that he's 'likely to miss', ESPN has him doubtful and cut his projection from 13.1 to 0.0. You already moved Jalen Coker into the flex at 09:30, and that's what the projection wants. But Coker is questionable himself, and Carolina elevated receiver Ja'seem Reed from the practice squad this afternoon. With Justin Jefferson out too, there's no healthy receiver left on your bench. ESPN has it 124.7 to Aye-Aye's 125.0, 50%.

One check left, and it's late: Carolina's inactives at 16:50 on Sunday. If Coker is out, Alvin Kamara takes the flex; he plays Monday night and has no injury listing. Nothing to do before then, and nothing to do tomorrow morning: the 06:00 London check is no longer yours to make.

case.label: The risk
case.body: Coker's 13.0 is the number most likely to be wrong. He didn't practise Wednesday and was limited Thursday and Friday; Canales wanted to keep evaluating him through the weekend (Panthers.com, 3 Oct). Carolina put Xavier Legette on injured reserve and elevated Ja'seem Reed this afternoon. SI's Panthers site reads the elevation as trouble for Coker; Legette's move alone also explains it, so it's a hint and not a ruling. Carolina have their bye next week, which is a reason for them to be careful.

case.label: Their side
case.body: Aye-Aye start Herbert (12.6), McCaffrey (20.3), Jeremiyah Love (15.6), Kyren Williams in the flex (13.1), St. Brown (20.2), McMillan (15.0), Tyler Warren (13.1), the Eagles D/ST (6.2) and Aubrey (9.0). Aaron Jones (18.1) still sits on their bench behind Williams: if they fix that, their number goes up five. Two of today's items help them: Keenan Allen was ruled out for the Colts (Rapoport; Field Level Media, 3 Oct), which pushes targets toward Warren, and McMillan plays in the same game as your Coker.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Coker inactive at 16:50 Sunday: Kamara into the flex. Coker active: the lineup stands as set.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only · check Carolina's inactives Sun 16:50 Mexico City; the flex locks at 18:20
doFirst.title: If Coker is inactive: Kamara into the flex
doFirst.subtitle: You've already made the McLaurin swap. Coker is questionable with a quad and Carolina called up a receiver today. Kamara plays Monday and is the only cover left.

case.label: The injury
case.body: Quad. No practice Wednesday, limited Thursday and Friday with individual work and limited team reps; still questionable, and Canales 'wanted to continue to evaluate him throughout the weekend' (Panthers.com, 3 Oct, 16:00 ET). The same post put Xavier Legette on injured reserve and elevated WR Ja'seem Reed. SI's Panthers site says Canales had tied a Reed call-up to Coker not playing; I couldn't find that quote at source. ESPN still has Coker at 13.0, so none of today's news is in the number.

case.label: Why Kamara
case.body: By 16:50 on Sunday he's the only player on your bench who hasn't kicked off. He isn't on the Saints' Saturday report at all, with no game status (NewOrleansSaints.com, 3 Oct). He projects 10.6, against Atlanta, who've allowed the 2nd-fewest points to backs (footballdb). It's a fallback, not an upgrade.

case.label: Why not move now
case.body: Coker projects 2.4 above Kamara and nobody has ruled him out. Leaving him in costs nothing: his game is the last one on Sunday and Kamara's is on Monday, so the swap is still open after the inactive list.

case.label: Who is throwing
case.body: Bryce Young, no designation. He threw 48 times in Week 3 under pressure on 56% of dropbacks (Sharp Football, 1 Oct). Kamara has Tyler Shough, who isn't on the Saints' report.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: It fires and Kamara scores less than the best alternative you could still have started at that moment. If Coker is active it never fires.

whatWentWrong.title: McLaurin went from game-time decision to doubtful in a morning
whatWentWrong.lead: 13.1 at 07:00, 0.0 by the afternoon. The swap the brief wrote for 06:00 Sunday was needed a day early, and you made it.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Ben Standig: 'Despite initial hope he would play through a hamstring injury', McLaurin 'is now likely to miss Sunday's game in London' (via Heavy and Yahoo, 3 Oct). RotoWire has him expected to miss. I couldn't open a Commanders announcement; ESPN's doubtful tag and its 0.0 are what the league file shows.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The card above. With Jefferson and McLaurin both down, Coker is the last receiver, and behind him the flex is a running back.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin active at 06:00 Sunday against every report. He'd be locked on your bench by then anyway; don't chase it.

whatWentWrong.title: Two of five receivers are out and the third is questionable
whatWentWrong.lead: Jefferson out, McLaurin doubtful, Coker questionable. The bench is three running backs and two injured receivers.

case.label: The evidence
case.body: Jefferson didn't practise all week and O'Connell says Minnesota won't rush him (Vikings.com, 2 Oct). Heavy reports Washington hope to have Jayden Daniels back in Week 5; nobody has put a date on McLaurin.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing today: the free receivers (Meyers 10.8, Washington 10.3, Raymond 9.8) all project at or below Kamara's 10.6, so adding one doesn't improve tomorrow's flex. It's Tuesday's question, when Metcalf and Boston clear.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A multi-week timeline on Jefferson or McLaurin before Tuesday: then Monangai's seat goes to a receiver.

worthALook.name: DK Metcalf
worthALook.lead: 88% rostered everywhere else and unowned here. He can't be added before Wednesday, so this is Tuesday's decision.

case.label: The role
case.body: 9 targets, 5 catches, 115 yards and 16.5 points Thursday (Week 4 live archive) on 62 snaps, 97%, with 136 air yards, 36% of Pittsburgh's (RotoWire box-score breakdown 2 Oct). 10, 9, 5, 9 targets over four games (archive). Michael Pittman Jr. drew 4 targets on 47 snaps beside him.

case.label: The number that kills it today
case.body: He has already played Week 4 and is locked on waivers until Wed 7 Oct, 01:00 Mexico City. ESPN projected him 10.1 this week, and the waiver tool's only question this run is Denzel Boston, not him.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Tuesday's run, before claims process. Chem's priority resets weekly, so the claim costs nothing lasting. The drop would be Monangai: Swift is cleared, so he's a ten-carry backup. With Jefferson and McLaurin both hurt, a healthy receiver is worth more to this roster than it was this morning.

doNotChase.name: Malik Washington
doNotChase.lead: New on the list: Miami's most-targeted receiver, in the league's worst offence.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 8, 5, 10 targets for 6.3, 8.7 and 11.1 points (archive). He led Miami with 10 targets on 34 routes in Week 3, and Achane's injury moves motion and sweep work toward him (TWSN 29 Sep; Vikings.com 2 Oct).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 23 targets have produced 26.1 points in three games (archive): volume that scores little, from Malik Willis, whose passer rating is fourth-worst among qualifying quarterbacks (Vikings.com). Miami haven't scored more than 13 in a game, and you start the defence he faces. He projects 10.3, under Kamara's 10.6.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Ten-plus targets and 15 points at Minnesota tomorrow: then he's compared with Metcalf and Boston on Tuesday for Monangai's seat.

doNotChase.name: Kalif Raymond
doNotChase.lead: A free agent producing every week, with a backup quarterback expected to throw to him.

case.label: The rise
case.body: 9, 5, 7 targets for 16.4, 9.0 and 21.0 points (archive): a 20.4% target share and three red-zone targets (FantasyPros). The Week 3 game came from Case Keenum.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He projects 9.8, below Coker (13.0) and Kamara (10.6), so he doesn't reach your lineup even if Coker sits. Tyson Bagent is expected to start, his third quarterback in four weeks (Rapoport via Yahoo, 3 Oct), and Chicago lost their left tackle to IR today. The waiver tool didn't surface him because his opportunities fell from Week 1.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A second productive game with Bagent tomorrow: then he's part of Tuesday's comparison for Monangai's seat. He's a free agent, so nothing is lost by waiting.

doNotChase.sources: Week 1–3 archive · FantasyPros · Yahoo · Chicago Sun-Times

doNotChase.name: Jaylen Wright
doNotChase.lead: Cleared for Sunday after two full practices, and he's the man splitting Gordon's work.

case.label: The rise
case.body: Full Thursday and Friday, no designation. Hafley: 'should be good to go' (NBC Sports 2 Oct). Fowler: the two 'will share the load in the short term... for now Miami plans to use both' (via Yahoo, 30 Sep).

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: He'd be your sixth back, splitting a Miami backfield you already own half of, at Minnesota, who allow the 4th-fewest points to RBs (footballdb). 3 carries all season (archive). ESPN: 7.5 to Gordon's 9.0.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Wright takes over outright tomorrow (Gordon under 8 touches): then the Gordon claim is the thing to revisit, not a reason to own both.

doNotChase.sources: NBC Sports · Yahoo · footballdb · Week 1–3 archive

waiverAnalysis.summary: One question, and it's an artefact: the tool counts the injured Jefferson as your 'weakest movable' receiver, so Denzel Boston clears him. Three weeks of data, still thin. Nothing clears Monangai at running back. Same answer as this morning.

rising.name: Denzel Boston
rising.roleReason: Cleveland's lead outside receiver: 59 snaps (95%), a route on 92% of dropbacks and 148 air yards, 65% of the team's, on Thursday; 52% of Cleveland's air yards on the season (RotoWire 2 Oct). The role is real. The comparison isn't: Jefferson's 3.0 in Week 3 is an ankle injury on his seventh snap.
rising.action: WATCH — on waivers until Wed 01:00, and you dropped him Wednesday for Addison; Tuesday's run compares him with Metcalf for Monangai's seat

settled.title: 'McLaurin: a true game-time decision' (this morning's brief)
settled.result: By mid-morning he was 'likely to miss' (Standig) and ESPN had him doubtful at 0.0. The brief's swap was written for 06:00 Sunday; you made it today. Whether Coker was the right replacement is graded on Sunday's scores.

settled.title: 'Wright limited Thursday' (Thursday afternoon's brief)
settled.result: He was upgraded to a full practice (FantasyPros, NBC, RotoWire, CBS, 1 Oct). The brief went out about an hour after the report. Gordon's row is corrected: it's a split.

settled.title: Coker in the flex over McLaurin (21 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Coker 3.8, McLaurin 19.7 on the bench. Closed WRONG. It was also a coin flip that should never have had a thesis.

settled.title: Hold Likely through the Giants' quarterback change (22 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: 3.3 on 5 targets, so the under-six clause fired. Closed WRONG, not EXPIRED.

settled.title: Hold Pineiro over McPherson (23 Sep)
settled.result: Archive: Pineiro 8, McPherson 11. The written falsifier didn't fire, so it stays open, but the hold lost 3 points.

settled.title: Start Warren over Tuten (13 Sep, reviewed weekly)
settled.result: Archive: 20.6 to 17.0 in Week 3; 2 of 3 weeks won. Closed RIGHT.

settled.title: Let Kyle Pitts go; Chem can't use a second TE (23 Sep)
Decline Jaxson Dart at 83% owned (23 Sep)
settled.result: Out for the season with knee damage (Bleacher Report, 28 Sep). Closed RIGHT.

cannotSee.label: Coker's quad
cannotSee.body: Still questionable, with no report today on how he moved. Reed's elevation is a hint and Legette's IR move explains it equally well. The 16:50 Sunday inactive list is the first hard answer; it can't say whether he plays a full game.

cannotSee.label: McLaurin's status
cannotSee.body: 'Likely to miss' is one beat reporter, repeated by Heavy, Yahoo and RotoWire. I couldn't open a team announcement, and nobody has given a timeline past Sunday.

cannotSee.label: Reports I couldn't retrieve
cannotSee.body: Hogs Haven (McLaurin and Washington's elevations), Buffalo Rumblings, Pats Pulpit, Dawgs By Nature and Big Cat Country block me; ESPN's injury pages returned empty; RotoBaller returned navigation only. Several results were from past seasons (a 2025 'Coker expected to play', a 2025 Dolphins backfield note) and were discarded.

cannotSee.label: Quotes
cannotSee.body: This afternoon's pages were read through a summarising tool, so quoted wording is close but may not be exact.

cannotSee.label: Chicago's quarterback
cannotSee.body: Not announced. Rapoport expects Bagent; Ben Johnson says Sunday. One preview I read says Keenum. It touches Monangai, who is benched, and Raymond, who is a do-not-chase.

cannotSee.label: Minnesota's quarterback
cannotSee.body: The league file and this morning's reports have Kyler Murray; nothing I opened this afternoon named the starter. Addison's row rests on the morning read.

cannotSee.label: Matchup sample
cannotSee.body: footballdb's tables are standard scoring through Week 3; it has no PPR table. Allen's tile predates New England's absences in the secondary. The Vikings D/ST tile is a judgement from Miami's scoring, not a table.

cannotSee.label: Rival claims
cannotSee.body: ESPN returns only your own pending claims. Metcalf, Dowdle and Boston clear on Wed 7 Oct at 01:00 Mexico City; Meyers, Washington and Raymond are free agents anyone can add first.

cannotSee.label: The wire screen
cannotSee.body: wire_screen.py counts Week 4 as a stat week once one game is played, so its list is Steelers and Browns plus Tyler Higbee. Both passes returned the same eleven names as this morning, so the verdicts are carried. It can't see Holani, Lemon, Washington or Raymond; they're in do-not-chase from the ownership column.

cannotSee.label: Atlanta and Las Vegas
cannotSee.body: Kyle Pitts isn't on Atlanta's report and was on the field for 76% of dropbacks in Week 3 (Sharp Football); that isn't the snap share the decision log's test uses. For Tre Tucker I have only that he isn't on the Raiders' report.
